title: The ✨ **Generate Commit Message** action is not available when a workspace is backed by a virtual file system
body:
### Description

The ✨ **Generate Commit Message** action is not available when a workspace is
backed by a virtual file system, such as one opened with the **GitHub
Repositories** extension (`vscode-vfs://github/<owner>/<repo>`).

### Repro

1. Open any repo via **GitHub Repositories: Open Repository...**
2. Ensure Copilot Chat is installed, enabled, and signed in with an active subscription
3. Edit a file so there are pending changes
4. Open the Source Control view

**Expected:** the Generate Commit Message action appears in the SCM input box
toolbar, as it does in a local clone.

**Actual:** the action is absent. "Commit & Push" works normally, so the SCM
provider itself is functional — only the AI commit message action is missing.

No Copilot configuration changes this. It remains absent with Copilot Chat
enabled, signed in, and `github.copilot.enable` at defaults.

### Analysis

In a virtual workspace the SCM input box is owned by the GitHub Repositories
provider rather than the built-in Git extension, and the action appears to be
contributed only against the built-in Git provider. Confirmed via **Developer:
Inspect Context Keys** on the commit input — `scmProvider` is not `git` here.

### Why it matters

The GitHub Repositories extension is positioned for quick edits and reviews
without cloning — exactly the small, one-or-two-file commits where a generated
message saves the most effort. Today those are the only commits that can't have
one.

### Related

- #313051 — extensions cannot programmatically commit or invalidate the GitHub
  Repositories provider's SCM cache (same provider, adjacent integration gap)

body: Type: Bug **Summary** VS Code agents using the Fireworks provider fail because internal chain-of-thought metadata is forwarded inside a chat message. Fireworks rejects the request during validation. **Environment** Client: VS Code Agents / Copilot SDK Provider: Fireworks Model: glm-5p3-flash Error Failed to get response from the AI model; retried 5 times 400 invalid_request_error Extra inputs are not permitted: messages[2].cot_id messages[2].cot_summary The client surfaces the underlying Fireworks 400 as a 502 and retries unnecessarily. **Steps to reproduce** Configure a VS Code agent to use the Fireworks model. title: Inline suggestions (ghost text) never trigger for documents from third-party FileSystemProvider schemes (e.g. Code for IBM i "member:" scheme)
body:
### Summary
GitHub Copilot's inline completion (ghost text) provider does not produce suggestions for documents opened through third-party FileSystemProvider implementations using a custom URI scheme — for example, the "member:" scheme used by the Code for IBM i extension (https://github.com/codefori/vscode-ibmi) to expose IBM i source members as editable documents.

### Environment
Copilot / Copilot Chat extension: latest. Code for IBM i extension: 3.0.13. OS: Windows.

### Steps to Reproduce
(1) Install the Code for IBM i extension and connect to an IBM i host.
(2) Open a source member for edit (e.g. member:/GCLIB/QRPGLESRC/DEMO02.SQLRPGLE?readonly=false).
(3) Confirm the editor is fully editable, and the language mode (bottom-right status bar) matches the file type (e.g. "RPGLE"), same as an equivalent local file.
(4) Start typing code that would normally trigger a ghost text suggestion.
(5) Compare with the same edit performed in a local file:// document of the same language.

### Expected Behavior
Inline suggestions (ghost text) appear for the member document, consistent with local files of the same language and content.

### Actual Behavior
No ghost text ever appears for the member: document, regardless of editor.inlineSuggest.enabled, language-specific overrides, or content. The Copilot status bar icon shows no warning/error state — identical to when Copilot is working normally. The "GitHub Copilot Chat" Output panel shows zero log/event activity when editing the member: document, whereas identical edits in a local file produce visible request/response log entries. This suggests the inline completion provider's document filter/selector excludes the member: scheme (and likely any non-standard scheme outside an internal allowlist such as file, untitled, vscode-remote, vscode-vfs, vsls) before a completion request is ever attempted — it is not a network, auth, or settings issue.

### Impact
Any extension that exposes remote/virtual content as editable text documents through a custom FileSystemProvider (Code for IBM i, and potentially other remote-development or legacy-system extensions) cannot offer Copilot ghost text to users editing that content, even though the documents are fully valid, editable TextDocuments with correct language IDs. Copilot Chat (chat panel / inline chat) is unaffected since it doesn't rely on the same provider registration.

### Request
Please consider one of the following: expanding the inline completion provider's scheme allowlist to include documents from any registered FileSystemProvider; providing a documented extension API / setting that lets third-party filesystem providers opt in to inline completion support; or, if this is intentional (e.g., for telemetry/content-exclusion reasons), documenting the supported scheme list so extension authors and users understand the limitation.

### Additional Context
Diagnosed by confirming inlineSuggest is enabled and works for local files; language mode and editability are identical between local and member documents; and the Copilot Chat Output panel shows zero activity for member documents but normal activity for local files, indicating the request is filtered out client-side before ever reaching Copilot's backend.

title: Test: AHP sandboxing in Agents and Editor windows
body:
## Owner Assignment

- [ ] Windows @dmitrivMS
- [x] macOS @lramos15
- [x] Linux @TylerLeonhardt

Each OS owner covers both the Agents Window and Editor Window.

Complexity: 4

Authors: @dileepyavan 


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23335765%0A%0A&assignees=dileepyavan)

---

Verify sandbox enforcement, session isolation, setting precedence, and sandbox icon/toggle behavior for **Copilot Agent Host Protocol (AHP) sessions**, in both the **Agents Window** and the **Editor Window**, on **Windows, macOS, and Linux**.

**Scope:** AHP sessions only. Do not use extension-host/local Chat sessions or standalone CLI sessions as substitutes. The terminal sandbox toggle covered here is Copilot-specific; other providers' permission models, cloud sandboxes, and Dev Containers are not part of this item.

**About the changes :**
- The sandbox toggle enables or disables sandboxing for the current session only.
- New sessions initialize the sandbox toggle from the effective User/Workspace setting.
- Resumed or restored sessions retain their previously selected sandbox state.
- Managed settings take precedence over the local settings.

## Setup
- **Windows:** Install the September 8, 2026 security update applicable to your Windows version before testing:
  - **Windows 11 24H2 / 25H2:** [KB5124008 (OS Builds 26100.9445 and 26200.9445)](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/servicing/os/windows-11/2026/09/kb5124008-windows-11-24h2-25h2-security-update).
  - **Windows 11 26H1:** [KB5124012 (OS Build 28000.2954)](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/servicing/os/windows-11/2026/09/kb5124012-windows-11-26h1-security-update).
- Ensure `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` is false.
- Setup mock policy server following https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/.github/skills/policy-and-managed-settings/local-testing.md


## Test

### 1. Basic sandboxing

- Select any available permission mode and enable **Sandboxing for terminal** for the session. Sandboxing should work with any permission mode.
- Ask the agent to run a simple terminal command in the repository. Verify allowed operations succeed.
- Try accessing a denied test directory and making a network request with network access disabled. Verify both are blocked without silently running unsandboxed.
- Turn sandboxing off and retry the harmless test command, subject to normal OS permissions and tool approvals. Turn it back on and verify restrictions return without changing the selected permission mode.
- With sandboxing enabled, set `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands: true` and ask the agent to retry a harmless blocked command outside the sandbox. Verify a confirmation appears before the command runs unsandboxed.
- Reject the confirmation and verify the command does not run outside the sandbox. Retry and approve; verify it runs outside the sandbox only after approval. 

### 2. Session-level sandboxing

- Create sessions A and B without touching the toggle. Verify both initially inherit the applicable default.
- Turn sandboxing on for A and off for B. Alternate between the sessions and verify both the UI and actual terminal behavior remain independent.
- Change A's toggle before the first request and again between turns. Verify the next turn uses the selected state without recreating the session.
- Verify toggling a session does not modify User/Workspace settings or another session's selection. A new session C must inherit the default, not the last session's toggle.
- Reload the window, reopen A and B from history, and verify their explicit selections persist and are enforced. Repeat after restarting VS Code.
- Where peer chats/subagents are available, verify terminal work uses the owning session's sandbox choice and cannot escape a mandatory policy. An unrelated session must remain unaffected.

### 3. Setting hierarchy

With no managed policy, verify the toggle and actual terminal behavior match this table:

| Applicable default | Session selection | Expected sandbox state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off | Untouched / inherit | Off |
| On | Untouched / inherit | On |
| Off | Explicitly on | On |
| On | Explicitly off | Off |

- Turn sandboxing on in User settings and start a new session. Verify sandboxing is on.
- Turn it off in Workspace settings, where supported, and start a new session. Verify Workspace overrides User. Remove the Workspace value to fall back to User; remove both to use the product default.
- Change the session toggle. Verify it overrides the User/Workspace setting for that session only.
- Change the User/Workspace setting again. Sessions without an explicit selection should follow it; sessions with a saved selection should keep their choice, including after restore.
- If organization policy requires sandboxing without bypass, verify it stays on and the toggle is disabled, regardless of settings or saved session choices.
- If organization policy enables sandboxing but allows bypass, verify it starts on and can be turned off for the session. Mark policy checks as blocked if no test policy is available.

### 4. Sandbox icon and toggle

- Open the permissions picker in each window. Verify **Sandboxing for terminal**, its checked state, the shield indicator, and hover text agree with the effective sandbox state.
- Toggle on/off with the mouse and keyboard. Verify the UI updates without reopening the window and the next terminal command confirms the same state.
- Switch sessions, permission modes, and agent modes; reopen the picker and restore history. Verify no stale shield/toggle state, unintended permission changes, or cross-session state leakage.
- With `chat.experimentalModePermissionsPicker` both enabled and disabled, verify equivalent sandbox behavior in the combined and separate picker layouts.
- Under mandatory policy, verify the disabled toggle explains that sandboxing is required by the organization. With bypass allowed, verify the tooltip explains that it can be disabled.
- Verify keyboard focus/navigation and screen-reader labels convey sandbox state and whether the toggle is disabled. Check light, dark, and high-contrast themes for a visible, legible indicator.
- Hide the toggle using `chat.experimental.permissionsSandboxToggle.enabled: false`. Verify the control disappears without changing the saved session choice or runtime enforcement.

## Reporting

For failures, share the AHP logs and OS details (name, version, and build).

body:
Testing #335485

## Summary

The Agent Host running in the Node.js Dev Container did not have a Git author identity, even though Git identity was configured on the host.

This caused the initial Agent Host baseline checkpoint to fail and would also have prevented the requested commit.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.138.0-insider
- OS: Bluefin 44, Linux
- Docker Engine: 29.7.2
- Repository: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-remote-try-node
- Dev Container image: `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/javascript-node:1-18-bullseye`
- Container user: `node`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `user.name` and `user.email` in Git on the host.
2. Clone the Node.js Dev Container sample locally.
3. Start a new Agent Host session for the folder using **Dev Container**.
4. Ask the agent to modify files and commit the changes.
5. Inspect the in-container Agent Host log or wait for a Git operation.

## Actual Behavior

The initial Agent Host baseline checkpoint failed:

```text
git commit-tree <tree> -m "Agent host session <id> - baseline checkpoint" failed
```

Git reported:

```text
Author identity unknown

*** Please tell me who you are.

Run

  git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
  git config --global user.name "Your Name"

fatal: unable to auto-detect email address
```

The Git identity configured on the host was not available inside the Agent Host Dev Container.

The workflow could only commit after manually copying the host identity into the repository-local Git configuration.

## Expected Behavior

A Dev Container Agent Host session that is expected to create checkpoints and commits should have an appropriate Git identity.

Possible behaviors include:

- Inherit or safely forward the host's Git author configuration.
- Use the Dev Containers Git configuration forwarding mechanism.
- Ask the user to configure an identity before beginning the workflow.
- Avoid presenting the session as ready to commit when Git identity is unavailable.

The baseline checkpoint failure should also be surfaced to the user rather than appearing only as a warning in the Agent Host log.

## Additional Information

After configuring a repository-local Git identity, the agent successfully created:

- Branch: `private/health-endpoint`
- Commit: `169abd0`
- A clean working tree

The repository-local identity was removed after testing.

title: fix: centre the fork tooltip on the fork button
body: Fixes #335740 | Before | After | |---|---| | | | #335072 centred the fork glyph; this centres the tooltip. Three independent causes, each measured on a real hover in a running build. **1. The separator inflated the hover target — `chat.css`, −3.8px** The `·` was an in-flow `::before` on `.chat-fork-action-item`, so the managed hover anchored to a box spanning `dot + 4px gap + button`. It now draws in the item's left gutter (`position: absolute; right: 100%`, gutter reserved with `margin-left`), leaving the item's border box equal to the button — hover target width 36.71px → 29.14px, net layout shift **+0.44px**. `pointer-events: none` also makes the dot inert; it was previously a click target for Fork. **2. Caret rounding on odd tooltip widths — `hoverWidget.ts`, +0.5px** The hover is positioned unrounded (`target.center.x - clientWidth / 2`) but the caret was placed at `Math.round(hoverWidth / 2)`. Since `_x` is itself fractional, that rounding could never snap the caret to a device pixel — it only broke the centring. Removed on both axes. **3. Caret half-width vs `PointerSize` under zoom — `hover.css`, −0.25px** `PointerSize` (3) is treated as the caret's half-width, but its `1px` borders round down to whole device pixels under zoom, leaving a 5.86px box centred at 2.93px. Sizing it as a `border-box` 6px square keeps the centre at exactly `PointerSize` at any zoom. The `.locked` variant drops its `width/height: 4px` (which would now mean a 4px *border* box) and is visually unchanged. ### Verification Measured against each hover's real anchor element, every pointer tooltip now centres within **0.011px**, independent of width parity and zoom. Before: odd-width tooltips +0.5px, fork button −3.78px. Note: several controls anchor their hover to a parent rather than the visible `.action-label` (Toggle Chat uses `DIV.action-container`), so measuring the inner element reports a spurious ~0.5px. ### Tests `chatForkActionViewItem.test.ts` gains a case rendering the fork item as a **non-first** toolbar item so `:not(:first-child)` applies, asserting the item's box equals the button's box and the separator is out of flow and not hit-testable. ## Summary

Improve the reliability of bring-your-own-key (BYOK) chat providers in the Copilot extension. The changes cover credential migration, conversation preservation, reasoning capability discovery and request serialization, incremental tool-call delivery, and OpenAI-compatible response handling.

**This is a draft for scope and implementation review, not a merge-ready change.** There is no linked tracking issue yet. The branch contains several independently committed fixes and reasoning support changes; in accordance with the contribution guidelines, issue association and separation into focused PRs need to be resolved before requesting final review.

## Changes

### Credential migration and logging
- Wait for provider-group migration to succeed before deleting the legacy API key.
- Share an in-flight migration between callers, retain the source credential on failure, and allow a later retry.
- Handle migration failures initiated during provider construction without logging credentials.
- Omit invalid custom header values from warning messages.

### Conversation history and endpoint cloning
- Validate Responses state markers before trimming conversation history, including the zero-data-retention path.
- Match Gemini tool results to complete call IDs instead of deriving function names from ID prefixes; reject orphan results and conflicting function names.
- Preserve multiple nonempty Gemini system instructions in their original order.
- Clone nested token-limit metadata without mutating the original endpoint, preserving Azure authentication and OpenRouter routing.

### Reasoning capabilities and requests
- Centralize BYOK reasoning option resolution across supported providers, including default enabling, explicit disabling, and supported effort selection.
- Merge live model capabilities with known metadata, and expose applicable reasoning controls without treating missing metadata as an explicit capability value.
- Serialize provider-specific reasoning controls for Chat Completions, Responses, native Anthropic/Gemini, OpenRouter, and configurable OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- Reject unsupported explicit-disable requests instead of silently ignoring them.
- Forward visible reasoning independently of whether encrypted reasoning metadata is requested.

### Tool streaming and endpoint compatibility
- Forward tool-call start events and incremental argument updates through the language-model wrapper and contributed endpoint, before the final tool call is available.
- Accept non-streaming Responses JSON based on the normalized response content type. Process output in order through the shared completion infrastructure while retaining the existing SSE path and error handling.
- Resolve custom endpoint paths using structured URL parsing, preserving query strings, fragments, and explicit API paths; reject invalid URLs and unsupported schemes.

The branch has eight commits grouped by responsibility, including regression coverage and a Copilot changelog entry. All changed files are under `extensions/copilot`; package changes add configuration schema fields, not dependencies. Local installation changes and pnpm files are not included.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A — reproduced in isolated browser diagnostics with no extension host; not separately reproduced via the installed app's UI.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.138.0-insider, `7b7e49c83affacfac726040280da69b4999f3e01` (2026-09-11). Diagnostics used `33a6a088236067e1a16d08481d617dfcf6da2e2c`; affected code is identical.
- OS Version: macOS 26.6.2, arm64; headless Chromium diagnostics.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In a browser harness, create a real compact `MultiDiffEditorWidget` at 900×640 with 90 two-sided text diffs, real model services, and a synthetic text-model resolver. Collapse all before attaching the view model with `preserveFocus: true`.
2. Collapse/expand five times, allowing two animation frames between operations, then call `widget.setViewModel(undefined)` and dispose the input.

**Observed:** teardown reports `Cannot unbind a diff editor template from a different item` (11 occurrences in the diagnostic run). This was found during investigation; the original Insiders renderer log did not contain this error.

**Cause:** [`ManagedVirtualizedItem._clearBinding`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/7b7e49c83affacfac726040280da69b4999f3e01/src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/virtualizedItemManager.ts#L225-L247) leaves its template reference/current binding exposed while disposing the binding. The captured synchronous chain is:

```text
_clearBinding -> DiffEditorItemBinding.dispose -> template.unbind
  -> setItem(undefined) -> editor.setDiffModel(null)
  -> CodeEditorWidget.onEndUpdate -> observable reaction
  -> _clearBinding -> same binding.dispose -> template.unbind throws
```

The inner call sees an already-cleared template view model, but binding disposal is not yet complete; the binding's `isDisposed` guard cannot prevent re-entry.

**Expected / fix direction:** release each binding and return its template exactly once, without teardown errors. Make release re-entrancy-safe through an explicit releasing state or atomic lifecycle transition, preserving cleanup ordering rather than suppressing the assertion. A temporary `_clearBinding` re-entrancy guard eliminated all 11 errors.

Add regression coverage using the real model-detachment/observable callback path; a passive mock binding misses the re-entry. This is separate from #206959: the listener-count warning remains after this lifecycle problem is removed.

Relevant lifecycle history: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/10de1b9343662a4043258b418630481e27c863b1 (@hediet).

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A — reproduced in isolated browser diagnostics with no extension host; not separately reproduced via the installed app's UI.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->

- VS Code Version: 1.138.0-insider, `7b7e49c83affacfac726040280da69b4999f3e01` (2026-09-11). Diagnostics used `33a6a088236067e1a16d08481d617dfcf6da2e2c`; affected code is identical.
- OS Version: macOS 26.6.2, arm64; headless Chromium diagnostics.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In a browser harness, create a real compact `MultiDiffEditorWidget` at 900×640 with 90 two-sided text diffs using `MultiDiffEditorInput`, real model services, and a synthetic text-model resolver. Collapse all before `setViewModel`, yielding about 20 row templates.
2. Keep the widget alive. Call `setViewModel(undefined)`, dispose the input, load another 90-file input, and repeat three times. Count `.multiDiffEntry` elements after each clear.

**Observed:** retained row DOM grows **20 → 35 → 50 → 65**. Each cleared state has zero text models and only five cached templates/ten live label listeners. Disposed rows remain attached until the entire widget is disposed.

**Expected:** disposed templates remove their DOM; only the five intentionally cached templates remain after clearing.

**Cause / fix direction:** [`DiffEditorItemTemplate` appends its root](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/7b7e49c83affacfac726040280da69b4999f3e01/src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/diffEditorItemTemplate.ts#L287) but never removes it on disposal. The [pool disposes excess templates](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/7b7e49c83affacfac726040280da69b4999f3e01/src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/virtualizedItemManager.ts#L251-L293), leaving their DOM behind. Register root removal with the template's lifetime, **not** with unbinding, since pooled templates are reused. A temporary isolation experiment kept retained DOM at five across the same cycles.

Add regression coverage for DOM counts after repeated input replacement and pool eviction. This is actual DOM retention, distinct from the bounded listener-count warning in #206959.

Relevant pool/lifecycle history: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/10de1b9343662a4043258b418630481e27c863b1 (@hediet).
